title: Marina Square mall to close in March 2027 for redevelopment
Self-claimed wealth gurus in Singapore who drove Lamborghinis now made bankrupt
Marina Square to transform into 'hyper-mixed' 24/7 destination with living, hospitality, office, retail, sports, wellness, culture: SingLand
article:
Singapore Land Group (SingLand) on Sept 1 announced details of how it will partially redevelop and reposition the Marina Square complex on Raffles Boulevard, with the project slated for completion by 2031.

The 9.2ha complex will be turned into what the property investment and development group calls Singapore's first "hyper-mixed" development — with urban living, hospitality, workplaces, retail, sports, wellness and culture, all within a connected 24/7 destination.

Three new towers — a 204-unit luxury condo, a mixed-use block with a new 304-key hotel and offices, and 260-key serviced apartment block — will be integrated with the site’s three existing hotels: Pan Pacific Singapore; Parkroyal Collection Marina Bay, Singapore; and Marina Oriental, Singapore.

The trio of existing hotels will remain fully operational throughout the works.

The four-storey retail mall will undergo a comprehensive asset enhancement initiative across more than 76,000 sq m (818,057 sq ft) of gross floor area (GFA). Its refreshed offerings will include a broader mix of F&B, sports, wellness and lifestyle concepts, as well as landscaped and pet-friendly environments.

Marina Square Shopping Mall will close on March 31, 2027, to facilitate construction.

Designed by UK-based PLP Architecture and Singapore firm DP Architects, the project will capitalise on the site’s recent GFA uplift to about 362,493 sq m.

SingLand said it received a grant of written permission under the URA’s Strategic Development Initiative (SDI) on Aug 31. Under the SDI scheme, the site will realise an increase in GFA to around 362,493 sq m, excluding bonus GFA for balconies and indoor recreation spaces.

The redevelopment will introduce luxury residences, serviced apartments, premium Grade A offices, public parks, arts and cultural spaces, as well as sports and wellness facilities.

A sheltered walkway at the first storey and an elevated botanical loop will connect pedestrians to One Raffles Link , Millenia Walk , Suntec City and the upcoming NS Square.

Among the three new towers will be a 19-storey mixed-use block, within which a 304-key hotel will sit on levels four to 10, alongside shared spaces for networking, events and social interaction.

On levels 12 to 19 of this mixed-use block will be the office component with some 13,000 sq m of premium Grade A net lettable area, with views of Marina Bay, War Memorial Park and the Civic District.

Meanwhile, a new 24-storey serviced apartment block will house 260 keys with panoramic views towards Marina Bay and Bay East Garden.

Operators for both the new hotel and serviced apartments have yet to be appointed. SingLand said that together, the five hospitality assets at the complex will serve a wider range of guest profiles, stay patterns and lifestyle needs.

In addition, a 49-storey residential tower with a height of more than 190m will introduce 204 large-format luxury homes, ranging from three- to five-bedroom apartments and penthouses.

At the same time, the Marina Square project will look to create a more open and inclusive public realm.

The area above Stamford Canal, located along Raffles Avenue, will be transformed into a 6,500 sq m public park with planting, playscapes and event spaces.

There will also be a network of spaces for placemaking and social activity. These include more than 4,000 sq m of privately owned public space connected to the upcoming NS Square; The Cube, a 700 sq m event venue on Raffles Boulevard, and The Oculus, a 300 sq m central atrium within the mall.

Jonathan Eu, CEO of SingLand, said: "By adding residences, serviced apartments and workplaces alongside the existing hotels — and repositioning the mall around experience-led retail, sports, wellness and community — we are creating a new ecosystem where people can live, work, stay and connect."

He added that this "hyper-mixed" approach is about designing different uses to reinforce one another, with the mall and public realm serving as shared platforms for activity throughout the day.

The project also incorporates sustainability measures. For instance, the three new buildings will target the Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification. A satellite plant connected to the Marina Bay district cooling network will provide energy-efficient cooling to the development and surrounding buildings.

Singland added that the existing mall structure will be adaptively reused, as the whole-life carbon strategy extends to embodied emissions too.

Completed in 1986, Marina Centre was the first district developed within the wider Marina Bay area, combining offices, hotels and retail.

title: MediaTek shares soar 10% after blockbuster Nvidia investment
article:
(Sept 1): Shares of MediaTek Inc soared after the Taiwanese chipmaker scored a US$3.5 billion outlay from Nvidia Corp, the American chipmaking giant’s largest ever direct investment outside the US.

The deal announced on Monday will see Nvidia buy bonds convertible into MediaTek shares. MediaTek shares jumped 10% in Taipei on Tuesday, hitting a daily limit.

The Taiwanese company was once best known for its rivalry with Qualcomm Inc in the mobile phone market, vying for orders from the likes of Xiaomi Corp and Oppo. But it has gradually shifted its focus to designing custom silicon, taking on the likes of Broadcom Inc and gaining credibility as a partner to major tech firms seeking to build their own AI chips.

“This investment is a significant strategic endorsement of MediaTek,” said Francis Tan, chief strategist at Indosuez Wealth Management in Singapore. “It reinforces MediaTek’s evolution from being primarily associated with smartphone chips into a much broader AI semiconductor company.”

MediaTek earlier this year secured a partnership with Alphabet Inc’s Google, and some analysts have speculated that SpaceX could be its next AI customer. That momentum has led the chipmaker’s market value to roughly triple in recent months.

See also: Anthropic seals US$35 bil cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda — Bloomberg

Nvidia’s investment is part of a US$3.9 billion US dollar-denominated convertible bond sale by MediaTek, according to terms reported by Bloomberg News earlier on Monday. Alphabet and other investors also participated in the round, a spokesperson for MediaTek said in a separate statement, without specifying the investment amounts.

MediaTek CEO Rick Tsai said that he expects the company’s AI chip business to accelerate after the Nvidia deal. Previously the company guided its custom AI silicon business will reach US$2 billion this year, while saying it’s looking to secure 15% of the $80 billion segment in 2027.

title: UOB Private Bank appoints Dominique Boer as regional market head for Asean
article:
Boer, who was most recently at UBS as business sector head, private wealth and Australia International, UBS global wealth management Asia Pacific (APAC) and Singapore location head, internal markets APAC and global financial intermediaries APAC, will be based in Singapore. She will report to Chew Mun Yew, head of UOB Private Bank.

In her role, she will lead the growth and strategic development of the bank’s Asean franchise focusing on deepening client relationships, strengthening market leadership and accelerating growth across the region.

“As wealth creation accelerates across Asean, UOB is continuing to invest in its wealth franchise to capture the opportunities emerging from the region's growing affluent and high-net-worth segments,” says the bank in a statement dated Sept 1.

See also: Mapletree Industrial Trust’s CEO Ler Lily to become Mapletree Investments’ group CFO

“UOB Private Bank is well-positioned to support clients through increasingly complex investment, financing, succession and legacy decisions. By combining deep advisory expertise with comprehensive wealth capabilities, the bank helps clients preserve, grow and transfer wealth across generations,” it adds.

Boer’s appointment will be effective from Sept 17.

title: Asian data centre debt binge hitting banks’ limits, Barclays says
article:
(Sept 1): The billions of dollars being borrowed to fund data centers in Asia are pushing banks to their limits and making them more selective about which projects to finance, according to senior bankers at Barclays Plc.

Andrew Ashman, whose department helps companies secure loans, said in an interview that Asia-Pacific lenders “are reporting to be heavily exposed to the data centre sector.” As a result, banks are likely to favour familiar borrowers or deals that offer higher returns, said Ashman, who heads Barclays’ Asia-Pacific loan syndicate team.

Data centre loans in the region have surged to nearly US$29 billion ($36.9 billion) since the start of last year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. They’ve hit a record US$15 billion so far this year, a 27% jump from the same period in 2025. And there’s more to come, with Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers Ltd in talks to double an existing loan to as much as US$7 billion in what would be Asia’s largest data centre debt financing.

There are signs that banks are reaching their data centre sector limits and are looking for ways to free up capacity for more lending or pass on some of their risk. Credit Agricole CIB sought to offload a portion of a data centre loan in Hong Kong, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg in July, while Morgan Stanley explored using a significant risk transfer to hedge its exposure.

Data centre operators in Asia, like their American counterparts, are turning to capital markets to raise new funds. Sales of asset-backed securities in the US rose last year to the highest level in a decade, with offerings by fibre-infrastructure companies and data centre owners jumping 86% to about US$23 billion.

“We’re looking at ways in which clients can recycle that capital into long-term bond markets like ABS and project bonds, as has been done globally,” said Richard Satchwell, Barclays’ head of capital markets financing for Asia-Pacific. “The bank market can’t absorb the quantum of liquidity that’s likely to be required in the data centre space.”

See also: Festive cheers and new recycling scheme cast spotlight and shadow on beverage producers

title: Anthropic seals US$35 bil cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda — Bloomberg
article:
(Sept 1): Anthropic PBC agreed to a US$35 billion computing deal with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia Corp, part of an effort to quickly expand its AI capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Infrastructure company Hut 8 is developing the Texas data centre involved in the project, said the person, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. The Wall Street Journal previously reported on the agreement, saying that Nvidia would hold the lease on the data centre, which is in Nueces County, Texas.

The deal is just the latest AI computing agreement tied to Nvidia, the world’s most valuable business and the leading provider of AI chips. The company has been using its financial resources to expand access to computing infrastructure, which, in turn, should increase demand for its technology.

Anthropic, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the most significant customers for data centre power. The Claude chatbot maker last week agreed to spend US$45 billion to rent capacity from Nscale in West Virginia. In recent months, it has also signed cloud deals for US$50 billion with neocloud Fluidstack Ltd and US$45 billion with Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

A representative for Anthropic declined to comment. Nvidia, Lambda and Hut 8 didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

Lambda is in talks to raise as much as US$3 billion, Bloomberg reported last week. The company has discussed a valuation of as much as US$12 billion or more, according to people familiar with the talks.

See also: Nvidia to invest US$3.5 bil in chipmaker MediaTek

Lambda raised more than US$1.5 billion in a November funding round. The company also reached an agreement with Microsoft Corp last year to deploy AI infrastructure that would be powered by tens of thousands of Nvidia processors.

title: Malaysia bonds lag peers in August on supply, rate-hike concerns
article:
(Sept 1): Malaysian bonds delivered Southeast Asia’s worst performance in August as concern over the supply of long-dated notes and the risk of an interest-rate hike made investors cautious.

The yield on 10-year bonds jumped 16 basis points last month, the most in almost two years, and higher than the advance seen in Thailand and Singapore. Yields on similar-maturity debt in the Philippines and Indonesia declined at least 10 basis points each.

“Selling has been more persistent than we had expected,” said Winson Phoon, head of fixed‑income research at Maybank Securities in Singapore. The curve has “bear-steepened in recent weeks,” weighed down by supply, including the auctions of the 20- and 30-year bonds, caution over Treasury duration, as well as the risk of policy rate normalisation, he added.

Malaysia’s economy grew faster than initially estimated in the second quarter, data released mid-August showed, fuelling expectations of a rate hike. Ringgit swaps almost fully priced in a 25-basis-point increase by the central bank over the next 12 months just days after the release of the data.

A boom in semiconductor exports tied to the artificial intelligence boom, and strong domestic demand, have helped the economy counter the impact of the war in the Middle East. Bank Negara Malaysia has left its benchmark rate unchanged since cutting it to 2.75% over a year ago.

See also: UOB prices EUR1 bil worth of Euro-denominated dual-tranche covered bonds

The 16-basis point jump in Malaysia’s 10-year yield compares with an average decline of about 10 basis points in yields on similar-dated bonds for Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines and Singapore, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The 26-basis point gap is the widest since at least January 2020.

Fesa Wibawa, an investment manager at Aberdeen Group, said he sees “the recent sell-off mainly as a supply, positioning and relative-value adjustment, rather than a significant reassessment of Malaysia’s outlook.”

title: Keppel DC REIT announces placement and acquisition of two Tokyo data centres
article:
Keppel DC REIT has announced a private placement to raise not less than $600 million, pricing new units between $2.096 and $2.142. Keppel DC REIT last traded at $2.20. Its June 30 net asset value (NAV) is $1.67 and 1HFY2026 distribution per unit (DPU) was 5.713 cents.

The capital raising is to partially fund a new acquisition in Japan. Keppel DC REIT and Keppel have indirectly entered into agreements with unrelated third-party sellers to collectively acquire 90% effective interests in Tokyo Data Centre 4 and Tokyo Data Centre 5, two freehold, hyperscale fully-fitted (colocation) data centres located in Inzai City, Greater Tokyo, Japan.

Upon completion, Keppel DC REIT will hold an 88.62% effective interest in each data centre, while Keppel, through its interest in Keppel Japan KK, will hold a 1.38% effective interest.

The existing operator, an established global data centre owner and operator, will retain a 10% interest in each data centre, ensuring alignment of interests and operational continuity.

The aggregate purchase consideration (on a 100% basis) is JPY190.0 billion (approximately $1,548.5 million), representing an approximate 2.1% discount to the assets’ valuation of JPY194.0 billion (approximately $1,581.1 million).

Keppel DC REIT will pay approximately JPY168.4 billion for its 88.62% effective interest in the two data centres. The acquisition is expected to be immediately DPU accretive.

See also: Adrian Chui to step down as CEO of ESR-REIT

On a pro forma basis, if the acquisition were completed on Jan 1, 2025, DPU for FY2025 would increase by 2.6% from 10.381 cents to 10.649 cents.

The acquisition combines immediate DPU accretion with multiple avenues of long-term income growth. The assets benefit from contracted average annual rent escalation of approximately 2.8% and in-place rents are estimated to be at least 30% below prevailing market rents.

Weighted average lease expiry (WALE) is approximately 4.5 years for Tokyo Data Centre 4 and 10.6 years for Tokyo Data Centre 5, providing a balance between reversion opportunities and long term income visibility.

Located in Inzai City, one of Japan’s most established hyperscale data centre clusters, Tokyo Data Centre 4 and 5 are 100% occupied by four investment grade internet enterprise and IT services clients.

title: SingLand announces redevelopment of Marina Square; uplift in valuation to impact FY2026 NTA and EPS
article:
Singapore Land Group (SingLand) announced the “repositioning” of the Marina Square complex as “Singapore’s first hyper-mixed development” on Sept 1.

Three new towers will be integrated with the site’s existing John Portman-designed hotels — Pan Pacific Singapore, PARKROYAL COLLECTION Marina Bay, Singapore and Mandarin Oriental, Singapore — while the four-storey retail mall will be comprehensively renovated.

The project is designed by UK-based PLP Architecture and local firm DP Architects. The project will capitalise on the site’s recent gross floor area (GFA) uplift to approximately 362,493 sqm.

Based on the GFA, the cost of the extensive asset enhancement and new development is likely to be upwards of $2.3 billion. In February, DBS Group Research estimated the total cost to be $2.6 billion to $3.4 billion.

The redevelopment will introduce luxury residences, serviced apartments, premium Grade-A offices, public parks, arts and cultural spaces, and sports and wellness facilities. A continuous sheltered walkway at the first storey and an elevated botanical loop will strengthen pedestrian links to One Raffles Link, Millenia Walk, Suntec City and the upcoming NS Square.

“As Marina Bay enters its next phase, we have an opportunity to reimagine Marina Square as a more connected and compelling destination,” says SingLand CEO Jonathan Eu. “By adding residences, serviced apartments and workplaces alongside the existing hotels — and repositioning the mall around experienced-led retail, sports, wellness and community — we are creating a new ecosystem where people can live, work, stay and connect.”

See also: Strata shop unit at Nomu and three-storey conservation shophouse at North Canal Road for sale

This “hyper-mixed approach” is about “more than placing different uses together”, adds Eu. “It is about designing them to reinforce one another, with the mall and public realm serving as shared platforms for activity throughout the day. The project reflects our broader ambition to transform key assets into future-ready destinations that remain relevant to how people want to live and engage.”

A new 304-key hotel and 260- key serviced apartment will be introduced. The new hotel will cater to community-oriented living through shared facilities and curated programming, while the serviced apartment will serve longer-stay guests. Together, the five hospitality assets will serve a wider range of guest profiles, stay patterns and lifestyle needs.

The new hotel will occupy the fourth to tenth floors of the 19-storey mixed-use block, with shared spaces for networking, events and social interaction.

See also: Frasers Property acquires Cuppage Terrace for $175 mil

The 24-storey serviced apartment block will offer panoramic views towards Marina Bay and Bay East Garden across 260 keys. Operators for both hospitality components have yet to be appointed.

The office component will occupy the 12th to 19th floors of the new 19-storey mixed-use block, which provide approximately 13,000 sqm of premium Grade-A net lettable area (NLA), with views across Marina Bay, War Memorial Park and the Civic District.

The four-storey Marina Square Shopping Mall will undergo a comprehensive asset enhancement initiative across more than 76,000 sqm of GFA. The mall will be repositioned to become the common platform linking the precinct’s hotels, offices, residences, serviced apartments and public spaces. Its refreshed offer will include a broader mix of food and beverage, sports, wellness and lifestyle concepts, alongside landscaped and pet-friendly environments.

The 49-storey, 190m residential tower will introduce 204 large-format luxury homes, ranging from three- to five-bedroom apartments and penthouses. Residents will enjoy access to the wider hyper-mixed precinct’s hospitality, retail, wellness, culture and public space offerings.

The new residential, hospitality, office and retail components will be respectively held by the company’s indirect subsidiaries, which are wholly-owned by Marina Centre Holdings Private Limited (MCH) which is 77.33% held by Singland Properties Limited, and 22.67% held by the Company’s parent company, UOL Group Limited (UOL).

The group will procure an updated valuation of the site reflecting the approved Strategic Development Initiative (SDI) scheme, including the GFA uplift. Any resulting change in fair value, which will be non-cash in nature, will be recognised in the consolidated income statement of the group for FY2026 and will correspondingly affect the consolidated net tangible assets per share and earnings per share of the group for FY2026.

As the valuation exercise has not been completed as at the date of this announcement, the quantum of any such fair value change, and whether such change will be material, cannot be determined at this juncture, a SingLand announcement says.

Marina Square Shopping Mall will close on March 31, 2027 to facilitate construction. All three existing hotels will remain fully operational throughout the works. SingLand is working with relevant stakeholders to minimise disruption, maintain accessibility and provide clear wayfinding for hotel guests and visitors. The project is expected to be completed by 2031. Further details will be announced at key milestones.

title: Oil extends advance as US-Iran escalation revives Hormuz risks
article:
(Sept 1) : Oil pushed higher after the biggest gain in three weeks on Monday as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

West Texas Intermediate traded above US$86 after advancing 2.8% in the previous session, while Brent closed near $90 on Monday. US forces hit an island in Hormuz, while Iran retaliated with attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Jordan, the first exchange of fire in about a month.

Crude eked out a marginal increase in August after a volatile month, with prices buffeted by the stop-start efforts to end the war, including pledges by the US to cripple Iran’s economy. President Donald Trump dismissed concerns the conflict was draining American firepower, characterizing it as a “little war.”

“Traders reduced net crude oil positioning over the week as uncertainty persisted around the next phase of the Iran conflict,” said Bart Melek, global head of commodity strategy at TD Securities. “We continue to expect crude prices to move higher, as there are no signs that normal transit through the Strait of Hormuz will resume in the near term.”

Still, crude exports are moving through the narrow waterway, often on tankers with their transponders off to avoid detection. Persian Gulf producers including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq are all getting some barrels out.

title: August Focus: Macro Resilience, Micro Efficiency and Earnings Delivery
